page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per physical core. The server does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a high-speed 100 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory performance and single-threaded compression capabilities. The server achieves a strong rating in large-block memory bandwidth, with read-only speeds of 210.08 GB/sec and write speeds of 98.02 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 31.99 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (58922.47) and Geekbench multi-core (13676.0), fall into the average tier. LLM text generation performance is a notable bottleneck, with the medium 7B model achieving only 7.8 tokens/sec and the small 135M model reaching 40.51 tokens/sec, reflecting weak to poor performance in real-time text generation workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, x2iezn.metal represents a high-resource-density hardware class designed for enterprise workloads that require massive memory footprints alongside high single-core clock speeds. Because it lacks local storage and GPUs, the instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications that leverage network-attached storage. Ideal workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput caching layers, electronic design automation, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
